newsitem.title: USA: US pilot at least semi-conscious when he vanished.
newsitem.headline: US pilot at least semi-conscious when he vanished.

text.p: The pilot of an A-10 warplane missing in rugged Colorado mountain country was at least semi-conscious as he flew far off course but there is no way to know his intentions, an Air Force official said on Friday.

"There were manoeuvres made that required at least a semi-conscious pilot to make those turns," the official said, while denying suggestions that the Air Force believed the pilot intended to commit suicide by crashing the plane and its four bombs in Colorado last week.

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said there was no suicide note or other evidence that the pilot, Capt. Craig Button, 32, intended to kill himself, and no evidence of what his intentions were.
CNN quoted sources as saying Button appeared distraught after a recent meeting with his parents. It said his mother had joined the Jehovah's Witness religion.

The Air Force official said that if a reconstructed radar track of the plane's route was correct there was evidence the pilot had enough control of the plane to veer around cities after it left a three-plane formation in southern Arizona and headed north toward Colorado.

The plane has been missing since April 2 when it disappeared as it was flying behind two other tank-attacking A-10s toward a bombing range near Gila Bend in southwest Arizona. The radar track of what the Air Force believed to be the plane showed it flew north to Colorado and witnesses there said they believed they heard it south of the Vail ski resort.

Earlier this week, a group of cross country skiers on a nearby ridge reported hearing a loud boom, followed by a tremendous black cloud, but they never saw a plane. But an intense search of the area including overflights by a U-2 spy plane has not found a crash site.

The search has been hampered by heavy snow and severe cold, said Lt. Joanne Wright, a spokeswoman at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, which is coordinating the search. "It is suspected that if there is anything to be discovered it would be covered up at this point," she said. "They have had several feet of snow there."
Defence officials have said they had had no evidence of theft or sabotage in the disappearence of the plane that was loaded with four 500-pound conventional Mark 82 bombs.
